variants.name: Carved Stone
variants.detail: A squat, uneven, chipped slate-grey stone tablet, almost rectangular with beveled broken corners, small enough to hold. One deeply carved almond-shaped eye occupies the face: bold charcoal upper/lower lids, a simple recessed round iris and near-black pupil. The eye is an inscription cut directly into stone, with a single tiny muted ivory glint in its dark center. Rough grey stone, quiet ancient archaeological character, sparse broad chips. No jewelry fittings or frame.

variants.name: Forged Iron
variants.detail: A compact forged iron eye amulet: a horizontally angular hexagonal plate with two pointed ends and one uneven notch, silver-grey chunky metal. The face has a punched black almond aperture around a blunt dark iron circular pupil, framed by two thick mechanical-looking beveled eyelids. One tiny cold-white glint. A couple of large flat pixel highlights and a short dark groove communicate iron, without delicate engraving, chain, pendant bail, gemstones or gold. Practical heavy old smith-made object.

variants.name: Obsidian
variants.detail: A dark, narrow obsidian chip in an asymmetric elongated kite silhouette, diagonally tilted slightly. Mostly near-black with two broad muted violet-grey fracture planes, not shiny jewelry. A small horizontal almond eye is cut into its upper half, its recessed pupil entirely black and one short pale grey line along the upper eyelid. Strong chipped edges. A mysterious stone that has an eye inscribed on it, rather than an orb. No gemstone iris or colored circular lens.

variants.name: Fired Clay
variants.detail: A flat, warm rusty terracotta talisman, wide oval with flattened bottom and irregular worn edges. Thick primitive impressed eye mark pressed into the clay: almond outline in deep brown, simple round central depression. Three large stepped shading clusters suggest hand-shaped baked clay and a tiny chipped pale clay corner. Earthy russet, muted orange-brown and charcoal; no metallic casing, no gemstone, no green/purple magic orb. A portable ancient clay votive eye.

variants.name: Bone
variants.detail: A small aged ivory bone fragment carved into a broad almond shape with visibly asymmetric blunt tips. A hollow black eye socket in the middle has a thick pale rim and tiny dark pupil suspended like an old bone carving. One broad charcoal split at an edge, restrained warm ivory/grey/tan shading. Organic carved relic, compact strong silhouette, not a skull, skeleton face, eyeball, pearl or jewel. No ornate spikes or jewelry mount.

variants.name: Rootwood
variants.detail: A palm-sized piece of ancient rootwood with an asymmetric curled oval outline, one short hooked projection in the upper corner. The natural dark wood knot forms a bold almond eye with a black recessed pupil. Two broad brown grain bands follow the eyelid curve; one tiny desaturated moss-green patch at the bottom edge. A root or knot transformed into a talisman. Dark oak-brown, soft tan, charcoal, minimal green; no orb, jewel, green iris or golden frame.

variants.name: Hammered Gold
variants.detail: A very simple thin, dull antique-gold eye plate, horizontally wide almond silhouette with blunt corners and irregular hammered edge. The eye is punched into the metal: a charcoal iris recess and slit-dark pupil, with a thick asymmetric upper brow and only two broad warm ochre highlights. Flat archaic votive metalwork, almost like a small old coin cut into an eye shape. NOT a gold ring around an Ender Pearl, gemstone, glossy orb, luxury jewelry or shiny modern medallion.

variants.name: Flint
variants.detail: A triangular, irregularly flaked blue-grey flint arrowhead-sized stone, compact with one missing corner and three large flat faces. A very simple eye scratched diagonally across the broad flat face: off-white incised almond outline and a deep charcoal round pupil. The stone silhouette stays triangular, not eye-shaped. Broad rugged light/dark grey pixel clusters, understated pale etched mark, no magical glow, colored orb, metal frame or jewelry fittings.
